scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

So, the person in question is a 21-year-old woman who gave her two cousins, Tj (15) and Ked (13), iPhones when the new models were released. Ked had been stealing money from some extended family members, and he admitted to it. There was a fight, and Ked's parents defended him, not caring that he was stealing and cutting off the extended family. During winter break, Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents remained stubborn and narcissistic, refusing to admit they were wrong and hating the extended family now.

The extended family hosted a housewarming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to go, but their parents told Ked he couldn't go in case the extended family accused him of stealing again. Tj was told he could do whatever he wanted and that his parents trusted him to make the right decision. So, Tj went to the sleepover, while Ked stayed home.

When Tj arrived at the party, his phone started blowing up with texts from his parents yelling at him for coming to the extended family's house. They called him a disappointment, said they trusted him to make the right decision and he failed, and that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. Tj asked to be left out of the drama, but his parents repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home, they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for two weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he never got punished. The person is disgusted by how the parents are raising their kids and has lost all respect for them.

The person told the parents that while she can't control how they discipline their children, it's not their property to take away from him, and she won't go behind their back and let him use the phone. But since it was her gift to him, she'd like to hold onto it until the two weeks are up. The narcissistic parents made a big deal, and other extended family members are telling her she should've stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want. She's only asking for the phone to be in her possession because she thinks they're treating him unfairly. Everyone agrees the parents are horrible. If they were decent parents and punishing him fairly, she wouldn't have asked for the phone back. She may be the asshole because she asked for the phone back because she felt the parents were trying to establish dominance over Tj and control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules. She decided to take some of their "power" away by asking for her gift back.

Now, I need to evaluate whether her action is morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down.

First, the person gave the iPhone as a gift to Tj. Legally, once the gift is given, it's his property. However, since he's a minor, his parents might have some control over his belongings, depending on the laws and family dynamics. But morally, the person is asserting her right to take back the gift because she disagrees with how the parents are treating Tj.

The parents are using the phone as a form of punishment, grounding him and taking the phone away. The person feels this is unfair and cruel, especially since Ked, who actually stole money, wasn't punished. She's standing up for Tj, trying to protect him from what she sees as abusive parenting.

On the other hand, some might argue that she's overstepping by taking back the gift. The parents have the right to discipline their children as they see fit, even if others disagree with their methods. By taking the phone back, she's interfering in their parenting, which could be seen as disrespectful or meddlesome.

However, considering the context, the parents are described as narcissistic and stubborn, not admitting their wrongdoings, and treating their children unfairly. Tj is being punished for making an independent decision to attend the party, while Ked, who actually did something wrong, isn't being punished. This seems like a double standard and unfair treatment.

The person is trying to stand up for Tj, to protect him from what she perceives as harmful parenting. By taking back the phone, she's attempting to limit the parents' ability to control Tj through this punishment. She's not keeping the phone for herself but is holding onto it until the punishment period is over, which shows she's not trying to deprive Tj of the gift but is instead trying to prevent the parents from using it as a tool of control.

Additionally, she's not going behind the parents' backs to give Tj the phone; she's openly asking for it back. This shows she's not trying to undermine the parents covertly but is instead making her stance clear.

In terms of moral philosophy, this situation touches on themes of autonomy, justice, and the limits of parental authority. The person is advocating for Tj's autonomy by preventing the parents from using the phone as a punitive tool. She's also highlighting the injustice of the parents' actions, as Ked's theft went unpunished while Tj is being punished for making an independent decision.

However, there's also the aspect of respecting family boundaries. Some might argue that even if the parents are acting poorly, it's not her place to intervene in their parenting decisions. She could be seen as being too involved or as trying to control the situation, which could strain family relationships.

But given that the parents are described as horrible and that their actions are harmful, it could be argued that intervention is justified. She's not just intervening for her own satisfaction but is doing so to protect Tj from what she sees as an abusive environment.

Moreover, the person is not taking the phone back to punish Tj or to assert her own authority but to prevent the parents from using it as a tool of control. This distinction is important because her intention is protective rather than punitive.

In conclusion, while there are arguments on both sides, the person's action seems morally acceptable because she's standing up for Tj's well-being and autonomy, given the parents' unfair and harmful behavior. She's not overstepping in a way that's disrespectful or meddlesome but is instead acting to protect Tj from what she perceives as an unjust punishment.
